Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this — Vanguard Health is evaluating Redwood for a regulated AI workload that will handle PHI-level documents. We need help deciding between Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) and a Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) for this use case. High-level context:

- Primary workload: document summarization + structured extraction for patient intake forms and provider notes.
- Expected steady-state: ~40–60 RPS (requests per minute ~2400–3600), but peak spikes up to ~200 RPS during batch ingestion windows.
- Average model run: ~3.5k input tokens, ~250 output tokens.
- Latency target: P95 < 450ms for interactive flows (we accept some async for batch).
- Compliance requirements: SOC2 type II, data residency (US-only), customer-managed KMS, audit logs for every request.

Could you provide a sizing/architecture recommendation that ties to procurement options (committed Reserved GPU fleet vs Private deployment CAPEX + support)? We also need a rough cost delta and a proposal template we can share with our security/compliance and procurement teams.

I've attached our regulatory checklist and a short security FAQ (Attachment: vanguard-security-requirements.pdf).

Appreciate a quick initial read — can we get a 30-min sync early next week?

Regards,

Short answers up front:
- Both Dedicated and Private can meet SOC2 + KMS requirements. Dedicated will be faster to stand up and lower upfront for the short term; Private gives the tightest control over network ingress/egress and may be preferable if Vanguard requires on-prem air-gapped operations.
- For the load profile you shared we should size for steady-state concurrency and ~3–4x peak buffer for spikes.

To make our recommendation deterministic we need two quick clarifications (can you reply inline or in the attached template):
1) Typical concurrent user sessions during the interactive window (how many concurrent requests should we plan against rather than RPS).
2) SLA expectations for batch ingestion windows (how tolerant you are to warm-up/throughput smoothing).
3) Any hard constraints on egress (e.g., zero egress outside your VPC).

We've attached a one-page questionnaire to capture these (Attachment: initial-qry-template.xlsx). If it's easier we can take these in a 30-min call — I have availability Mon/Tue 13:00–16:00 PT.

Subject: Re: Vanguard Health — initial sizing assumptions and GPU calc

Thanks — did a short run of assumptions and back-of-envelope sizing. Notes and rationale below (feel free to copy into the external summary with the numbers we agree on).

Assumptions
- Avg request tokens in: 3,500; out: 250 => ~3,750 total tokens per request.
- Peak concurrent requests: we should plan for 60 concurrent interactive + 200 concurrent during batch spikes (these are different shapes; worst-case concurrency ~260).
- Effective batching/throughput: with continuous batching and KV cache efficiency we assume ~1.6x speedup for repeated prompts, but conservative plans should assume 1.0x for cold-starts.
- Target P95 latency < 450ms for interactive. We assume model = open LLM (e.g., LlamaX-70B fp16/quant), using optimized kernels.

Sizing (rough)
- Baseline interactive steady-state: 6 x A100-80GB (or equivalent) should handle ~40–60 steady concurrent requests with cached prefixes and batching, meeting P95 target on a tuned runtime.
- Peak buffer for ingestion windows: add 4 more GPUs (burst pool) to cover the 200 concurrent ingestion spike if Vanguard wants soft real-time ingestion; otherwise allow async batching to absorb the peak and keep the Dedicated pool smaller.
- Private on-prem: 4 nodes (each node = 2 x A100-80GB GPUs) with an HA replica and on-site orchestration for ~similar throughput; higher ops overhead and longer lead time.

Operational notes / constraints
- KMS calls per request: each encrypted object (if using customer-managed KMS for per-request keys) adds ~15–30ms depending on HSM latency; recommend caching envelope keys where policy allows.
- Audit logs: generating and storing per-request trace will increase egress/storage; design for a logging stream to a Vanguard-managed S3 with lifecycle rules.
- Network: Private deployments reduce cross-tenant egress but increase networking procurement (routers/firewalls).

Attached: detailed calc workbook with throughput rows and conservative/case estimates (Attachment: sizing-calcs-20270415.xlsx).

If we present both options, my recommended baseline for the external one-pager is: Dedicated — 8 reserved GPUs with 4-GPU burst; Private — equivalent compute (8 GPUs across 4 nodes) + onboarding fee. We can adjust to Vanguard's concurrency answers.

—Rishi

Subject: Redwood proposal summary — Dedicated vs Private (Vanguard Health)

Hi Asha — thanks again for the checklist and context. Per our internal sizing and commercial review, attached is a one-page summary and a short proposal document that maps to procurement requirements (Attachment: redwood-proposal-vanguard-20270416.pdf). Below is the executive summary and recommended next steps.

Executive summary (concise)
- Recommended initial path: Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with customer-managed KMS + US-only routing. Rationale: fastest to production (2–3 weeks), lower upfront than Private, supports SOC2 and audit logs, and we can configure strict VPC peering and egress controls.

Sizing we propose for the initial commitment
- Dedicated baseline: 8x A100-80GB equivalent reserved GPUs for steady-state interactive SLA.
- Burst pool: +4 GPUs for scheduled ingestion windows (auto-burst, billed on use).
- If Vanguard requires near-zero egress and full on-prem air-gap, move to Private: estimated 8 GPUs across 4 on-prem nodes with HA and replication; procurement lead ~8–12 weeks.

Compliance & operations notes
- KMS integration: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS/HSM; we recommend caching envelope keys where your security policy allows to avoid per-request HSM latency.
- Audit logs: we will stream request-level audit logs to your S3 bucket; retention and lifecycle policies are configurable.
- Rollout path: start Dedicated with strict controls + canary traffic. If additional network isolation is mandated later, we’ll migrate to Private with a staged data migration plan.

Next steps
1) Please confirm concurrent user estimates on the template we sent (we highlighted the fields we need).
2) Suggested pilot: 2-week Dedicated pilot with the configured reserved pool + daily syncs; we’ll instrument cost/latency telemetry.
3) If approved, Marissa will send the commercial terms and an initial 12-month commitment quote.

We’ve attached the proposal PDF and the internal sizing workbook for your procurement team to review. Happy to hop on a call to walk through the numbers — propose Tue 2027-04-20 14:00 PT if that works.

Best,
